{"concepts_used":["GC-0012","GC-0121","GC-0124"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMR1995/r4.4","quote":"(6) The goods and/or services must, as far as practicable, be specified in terms appearing in any listing of goods and services that is: (a) published by the Registrar; and (b) made available for inspection by the public at the Trade Marks Office and its suboffices (if any). (7) If any of the goods and/or services cannot be specified using terms referred to in subregulation (6), the applicant must provide sufficient information to enable the Registrar to decide the classification of the goods and/or services."},{"ref":"TMM/Part14/x-14.-annex-a13-list-of-terms-too-broad-for-classification/drinks","quote":"Suggested Alternatives Class 5: Medicinal drinks Class 29: Milk drinks Class 30: Coffee drinks Class 32: Non-alcoholic carbonated drinks"},{"ref":"TMM/Part14/x-14.-annex-a13-list-of-terms-too-broad-for-classification/carbonated-drinks","quote":"Suggested Alternatives Class 32: non-alcoholic carbonated drinks Class 33: Alcoholic carbonated drinks, except beer"},{"ref":"TMM/Part32B/2/4/2/4/3~2","quote":"Non-alcoholic beverages* (wide claim) Alcoholic beverages* (wide claim)"},{"ref":"TMR1995/r4.4","quote":"(2) The expression ‘all goods’, ‘all services’, ‘all other goods’, or ‘all other services’ must not be used in an application for registration of a trade mark to specify the goods and/or services in respect of which registration is sought. (3) The goods and/or services must be grouped according to the appropriate classes described in Schedule 1. (4) The applicant must nominate the class number that is appropriate to the goods or services in each group. (5) The groups must be listed in the order of their class numbers."},{"ref":"TMM/Part14/4/4/4","quote":"Would a proposed amendment widen the scope of the specification as filed? If so it will not be allowed under section 65 - see paragraph 4.8."}],"answer":"You need enough specificity to identify the goods and classify them—not necessarily a product-by-product list. That is a synthesis of the Regulations’ requirement to use published listing terms where practicable, or otherwise provide sufficient information for classification [1].

**Manual practice: avoid an undifferentiated claim to ‘drinks’.** The Manual’s annex of terms too broad for classification gives alternatives spanning classes 5, 29, 30 and 32, so drinks are not confined to classes 32 and 33 [2]. For carbonated drinks, it expressly suggests:
- **Class 32:** ‘non-alcoholic carbonated drinks’.
- **Class 33:** ‘Alcoholic carbonated drinks, except beer’ [3].

Those are examples for carbonated drinks, not a complete specification covering every kind of drink. Broader categories are also contemplated: the Manual’s goods-similarity discussion describes ‘Non-alcoholic beverages’ and ‘Alcoholic beverages’ as wide claims in its class 32/class 33 comparison [4]. However, that passage concerns similarity rather than approval of specification wording; the supplied passages do not establish the exact broadest acceptable wording for every drink you may intend to cover.

**Regulations—binding requirements:** group the goods by their appropriate classes, nominate each class number and list the groups in numerical order. Do not use ‘all goods’ or ‘all other goods’. Use the Registrar’s published terms as far as practicable; otherwise supply enough information to determine classification [1, 5].

**Drafting caution—Manual practice:** choose wording that captures the intended goods at filing. The Manual says a proposed amendment widening the specification as filed will not be allowed under section 65 [6]. This is the Manual’s statement about the Act; the relevant Act provision itself was not supplied."}
